source.title: Историческая справка
source.publisher: Khanty Mansi Mir (joint editorial office of the Khanty Yasang and Luima Seripos newspapers)

facts.text: Mansi rapper Yevgeny Anyamov, known as Bizzo, records his songs in Mansi and opened his own studio in his hometown of Ivdel to share his people's culture with youth.

nations.name: Nivkh
nations.lands: Lower Amur River in Khabarovsk Krai and Sakhalin Island, Russia

facts.text: The Nivkh speak a language isolate, probably one of the oldest languages of Eurasia. Its links to other languages have not been established.

source.title: Нивхи
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

facts.text: Nivkh life was built on fishing and hunting, including sea mammals taken with spears or with nets woven from leather straps.

source.title: Нивхи
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

nations.name: Udehe
nations.lands: Villages on the Khor and Bikin rivers in Khabarovsk Krai and Primorsky Krai, and towns of both regions, Russia

facts.text: Most Udehe today live in villages on the Khor and Bikin rivers in Russia's Far East.

source.title: Удэгейцы
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

facts.text: The Udehe language belongs to the Amur group of the Tungusic (Manchu-Tungus) languages.

source.title: Удэгейцы
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

nations.name: Nganasan
nations.lands: Southern and central Taimyr Peninsula, Krasnoyarsk Krai, including the villages of Ust-Avam, Volochanka and Novaya and the towns of Dudinka and Norilsk, Russia

facts.text: In August 2026, a state folk culture expedition in Taimyr met a knowledge keeper of Vadeyev Nganasan culture, who showed traditional dishes and how Nganasan cuisine differs from Dolgan.

source.title: Долганская юкола «кэрдиилээк» признана объектом нематериального наследия Таймыра
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

facts.text: Nganasan belongs to the Samoyedic branch of the Uralic-Yukaghir language family.

source.title: Нганасаны
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

nations.name: Sámi
nations.lands: Sápmi, across northern Norway, Sweden and Finland and the Kola Peninsula of Russia

facts.text: Norway's Sámi Parliament is elected by and among the Sámi. First opened in Karasjok in 1989, it now has 39 representatives from seven constituencies.
About 10,000 Sámi live in Finland, where three Sámi languages are spoken: Northern Sámi, Inari Sámi and Skolt Sámi.

source.title: About us | The Sámi Parliament of Finland

nations.name: Nanai
nations.lands: Lower Amur River valley in Khabarovsk Krai and Primorsky Krai, Russia, and the Sungari River area of northeast China

facts.text: Nanai communities also live in China, where about 4,600 Nanai were counted in 2000.

source.title: Нанайцы
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

facts.text: Clothing sewn from fish skin is a hallmark of traditional Nanai craft, rooted in a life of fishing on the Amur River.

source.title: Нанайцы
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

nations.name: Inughuit
nations.lands: Avanersuaq (the Thule region) in northwest Greenland, centred on the town of Qaanaaq

facts.text: Hunting is still a significant part of the livelihood of several families in Qaanaaq, Greenland's youngest and northernmost town.
The Inughuit have their own language, or dialect, and a hunting culture that is distinctive in several ways.

nations.name: Odul, Wadul
nations.lands: Kolyma River basin in the Republic of Sakha (Yakutia) and Magadan Oblast, Russia

facts.text: A Cyrillic-based writing system for Yukaghir was developed in the 1970s.

source.title: Юкагиры
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

facts.text: Today the Yukaghir speak two languages: Northern (Tundra) Yukaghir and Southern (Kolyma) Yukaghir.

source.title: Юкагиры
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

nations.name: Kalaallit
nations.lands: Kalaallit Nunaat (Greenland), which has self-government within the Kingdom of Denmark

facts.text: Under the Self-Government Act, in force since 21 June 2009, the people of Greenland are recognised as a people with the right to self-determination under international law.
The Self-Government Act recognises Greenlandic (Kalaallisut) as the official language of Greenland.

nations.name: Selkup
nations.lands: Between the middle Ob and Yenisei rivers: the Taz River area of Yamal-Nenets Autonomous Okrug and the Narym area of Tomsk Oblast, Russia

facts.text: Since a 2000 government decree, Russia has listed the Selkup as an Indigenous small-numbered people.

source.title: Селькупы
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

facts.text: Selkup belongs to the Samoyedic group of the Uralic language family.

source.title: Селькупы
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

nations.name: Taíno
nations.lands: Puerto Rico, Cuba, the Dominican Republic and other islands of the Greater Antilles, and diaspora communities in the United States

facts.text: Over about four decades a Taíno movement has grown in Cuba, the Dominican Republic and Puerto Rico, as more families and groups affirm their Native ancestry.

source.title: Taino: Native Heritage and Identity in the Caribbean
source.publisher: Smithsonian Institution (National Museum of the American Indian and Smithsonian Latino Center)

facts.text: Taíno community groups take part in language research, including tracing the Taíno roots of everyday words such as hurricane, hammock and tobacco.

source.title: This Culture, Once Believed Extinct, Is Flourishing

nations.name: Parikwene
nations.lands: The Urukauá River in the Uaçá basin of Amapá, Brazil, and Saint-Georges-de-l'Oyapock, Cayenne and the lower Oyapock in French Guiana

facts.text: Parikwene families have villages in both Brazil and French Guiana and travel across the border often to visit kin and to trade.

source.title: Palikur
source.publisher: Instituto Socioambiental (ISA), Indigenous Peoples in Brazil

facts.text: France recognizes Parikwaki, the Parikwene language, as one of the languages of France spoken in French Guiana.

source.title: Langues de France et langues régionales en Guyane: bilan au 7 décembre 2015
source.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, Direction des affaires culturelles de Guyane

nations.name: Yukpa
nations.lands: Sierra de Perijá on both sides of the border: Zulia state, Venezuela, and Cesar department, Colombia

facts.text: In Colombia, Yukpa resguardos are made up of settlements each led by a cabildo menor, with a cabildo mayor representing the people before the government.

source.title: Yukpa ywonku: Informe del estado de vitalidad de las lenguas nativas de Colombia

facts.text: Yukpa, a Carib-family language, has high vitality: in most communities speakers use it every day and make sure their children learn it.

source.title: Yukpa ywonku: Informe del estado de vitalidad de las lenguas nativas de Colombia

nations.name: Santa Rosa First Peoples Community
nations.lands: Arima, Trinidad, Trinidad and Tobago

facts.text: The community works to pass its culture on to younger generations and the wider public, serving as cultural ambassadors for Trinidad's First Peoples.

source.title: Celebrating Our First Peoples
source.publisher: National Trust of Trinidad and Tobago

facts.text: Trinidad and Tobago's government names the Santa Rosa First Peoples Community among the country's own Indigenous groups and holds a Day of Recognition every October 14.

source.title: Statement at the Special Permanent Council Meeting on the Commemoration of the International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples 2018
source.publisher: Ministry of Foreign and CARICOM Affairs, Government of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago

nations.name: Wai Wai
nations.lands: Kanashen in the far south of Guyana, and Indigenous lands in Pará, Amazonas and Roraima states, Brazil

facts.text: Waiwai, a Carib-family language, is the main language in Waiwai communities in Brazil, and most young people born there speak it.

source.title: Waiwai
source.publisher: Instituto Socioambiental (ISA), Indigenous Peoples in Brazil

facts.text: In 2007 the Wai Wai of Kanashen in southern Guyana made their titled forest a Community Owned Conservation Area; in 2017 it became a national protected area.

nations.name: Warao
nations.lands: Orinoco Delta of Venezuela, the North West District of Guyana, and communities in Trinidad and Tobago

facts.text: Trinidad and Tobago's government names the Warao Nation of Trinidad and Tobago among the country's own Indigenous groups.

source.title: Statement at the Special Permanent Council Meeting on the Commemoration of the International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples 2018
source.publisher: Ministry of Foreign and CARICOM Affairs, Government of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago

facts.text: In Guyana, where the name is spelled Warrau, Warao communities live in the wetlands of the North West District along the Barima and Pomeroon rivers.

source.title: Indigenous Nations
source.publisher: Ministry of Amerindian Affairs, Government of Guyana

nations.name: Tarëno
nations.lands: Southern Suriname along the Sipaliwini, Tapanahony and Paloemeu rivers, and the Tumucumaque Indigenous Park in Pará, Brazil

facts.text: Suriname's association of Indigenous village leaders counts the Trio among the country's four large Indigenous peoples, living mainly in the south.

source.title: Dorpen en Dorpsbesturen
source.publisher: Vereniging van Inheemse Dorpshoofden in Suriname (VIDS)

facts.text: In their own language the Tarëno say Wü Tarëno, 'I am Tarëno', meaning 'I am from here'; the names Trio and Tiriyó came from outsiders.

source.title: Tiriyó
source.publisher: Instituto Socioambiental (ISA), Indigenous Peoples in Brazil

nations.name: Patamona
nations.lands: North and South Pakaraima Mountains and the Essequibo region of Guyana, including villages near Kaieteur Falls

facts.text: Like their Ingarikó relatives, the Patamona use Kapon as a self-designation in the border region shared by Guyana, Brazil and Venezuela.

source.title: Taurepang
source.publisher: Instituto Socioambiental (ISA), Indigenous Peoples in Brazil

facts.text: Chenapou is the Patamona village closest to Kaieteur National Park, and Patamona communities hunt, fish and gather plants in the lands around Kaieteur.

source.title: In Guyana, Indigenous Peoples Fight to Join Conservation Efforts
